The proposed anonymization method raises the quantity of isomorphic neighbourhood networks by introducing fictitious edges into the social network graph. This means that a social network graph cannot re-identify a person based on their distinct local area network.

articleTitle: Parallel Implementation of Decision Tree for Online Fraud Detection using OpenMP, MPI and CUDA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: Online fraud detection is critical for ensuring the security of digital transactions. However, the growing volume of data and the need for real-time processing pose significant computational challenges. Traditional Decision Tree algorithms, commonly used for classification tasks, struggle to handle large datasets in real-time scenarios due to their computational complexity. This research addresses these limitations by parallelizing the Decision Tree algorithm to enhance its efficiency for online fraud detection. We leverage three parallel programming models—OpenMP for multi-core CPU processing, MPI for distributed systems, and CUDA for GPU acceleration to optimize the construction and evaluation phases of the Decision Tree. By distributing the computational workload across these architectures, we aim to reduce execution times while maintaining high classification accuracy significantly. A thorough performance evaluation compares the parallel implementations to traditional serial approaches, focusing on execution speed, scalability, and detection accuracy. The results reveal substantial improvements in processing speed, enabling real-time fraud detection without sacrificing accuracy. These findings provide valuable insights into developing faster, scalable, and more reliable fraud detection systems, contributing to enhanced security for financial transactions in an increasingly digital world.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis: A comparative Analysis of Machine learning models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: Sentiment analysis (SA) is the process of Finding or adding a meaning to a text using natural language processing, a deep examination of data that is maintained online at various platforms such as movie reviews, product reviews at different online shopping apps, twitter (now X), etc., to recognize and classify the opinions and ideas that are expressed in a certain passage of text. The process's aim is to search for the author's perspective on a certain topic, film, item, etc. The outcome can be neutral, bad, or good. There have been studies that demonstrated various methods in the SA methodology for gathering and analysing feelings related to the selected subjects’ polarity—positive, negative, or neutral. Social media SA is a reliable source of data and information. SA becomes significant in a variety of business, social, and academic fields. The evaluation and sentiment analysis process, however, is looked upon with difficulties. Finding the proper side of polarity and accurately interpreting sentiments that are hindered by these difficulties. Sentiment analysis is a part of natural language processing and used text mining to find and evaluate the bias from the text.

articleTitle: Delving Into Virtual Ventures and The Growing Vi-Gnettes of Vehicular Innovations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: New ways of getting around and virtual businesses are looked into in this study to get a better understanding of both of these topics. Please see below for a full picture of the "Virtual Innovation Optimization" (VIO) model. articleTitle: Violence Detection on Women using Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: Detection, prevention, and intervention strategies that rely on the application of state-of-the-art technology are required in that violence against women continues to threaten people from all walks of life. Through the applications of OpenAI's GPT models coupled with FastAPI for real-time deployment, this work comes to present an innovative solution in recognizing incidences of violence through Generative Artificial Intelligence. Through GPT's natural language capabilities, this system scans digital interactions for abusive language, harassment, and threats through social media and messaging platforms. Fast application programming interface (Fast API) is used by the system to give it scalability, real-time processing, and effective handling of concurrent requests so that it does not take too long in high-pressure situations. The technology is monitored and reports abusive behaviors through real-time alarm signals to the proper authorities or support services. Since it was trained on a wide variety of datasets, the model can both understand overt and subtle kinds of violence and thus be precise in identifying gender-based abuse that encompasses not only verbal manipulations but also psychological manipulations. This paper aims to deal with the ethical issues, problems, and possible impact of using a combination of GPT and FastAPI in relation to violence detection. The paper therefore underlines an integrated effort from AI developers, the legal frameworks, and social services to provide full mechanisms for protection.

articleTitle: Advancements in ECU Identification and Fingerprinting for Enhanced Cybersecurity in Vehicle Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: This paper explores novel techniques for identifying Electronic Control Units (ECUs) and detecting unauthorized messages in vehicle networks. By leveraging signal processing, machine learning, and spectral analysis, the proposed system achieves a high accuracy rate of 98.76% in classifying known ECUs and identifying rogue messages. Additionally, the paper discusses future research directions for dynamic online classification and network complexity optimization.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Based Collision Aware AI-Driven Intelligent Robotics Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: Learning-based robot navigation methods suffer from high data dependency and imperfect performance in specific environments, such as inability to walk straight in open spaces and high collision rates in densely cluttered environments. To enhance artificial intelligence (AI) driven robot navigation performance, a reinforcement imitation learning navigation method based on collision prediction is proposed. In the absence of a model, the state space, action space, and reward function required for the Markov decision process (MDP) are established based on the robot's performance. Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is utilized for training in a simulation environment, enabling the robot to navigate and avoid obstacles in multi-obstacle environments. Expert data is collected and used to continue training the policy using imitation learning methods to address the imperfections of reinforcement learning in both sparse and dense obstacle scenarios. A collision prediction model is designed, combining traditional control with deep learning. Based on the prediction results, the AI driven robot adaptively selects appropriate control strategies in different environments, greatly improving navigation safety. Through experiments, the proposed method's navigation performance and generalization ability are validated in numerous previously unseen scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhancing Flower Classification with a Deep Learning Approach Using VGG19 and ImageNet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: This paper aims to present an analysis on methods and advancements in floral classification techniques. The following research includes several techniques to investigates different approaches that can be used for categorization and picture analysis. Additionally, the main agenda for proposing this paper is to explore hyperparameter tuning and data augmentation techniques to enhance the workability of the model as well as to get to know how to use a reliable and precise image model on large datasets, such as the images of flowers in this case. The VGG19 model serves as the foundation to study architecture, and transfer learning is applied by utilising previously trained weights. Furthermore, the research examines approaches for data augmentation and hyperparameter tuning to improve the robustness and accuracy of the model. The outcome indicates significant improvements in the performance and accuracy, demonstrating the proposed methodology’s efficiency. The report concludes by highlighting drawbacks, which also includes suggestions for further directions and explore potential options to elaborate the scope of floral classification research.

articleTitle: A Comparative Review of Machine Learning Algorithms: Current State, Challenges and Future Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: The fundamental way to acquire information is through learning, which is the key indicator of human intellect. The primary method for making computers intelligent is machine learning. An important part of machine learning involves simulating human learning, studying, and improving performance and achievement using computers to acquire new skills, identify existing skills, and improve performance. Through the use of machine learning algorithms, which allow computers to see patterns and draw wise conclusions, we have completely changed how we handle and analyze data. Comparative studies are increasingly necessary to evaluate the current state of various algorithms, comprehend the challenges they encounter, and investigate their potential futures as the area of machine learning continues to grow quickly. Machine learning algorithms are studied in this paper from a comparative perspective, covering their current state, challenges, and future prospects. This study seeks to offer academics, practitioners, and decision-makers insightful information and recommendations for choosing the most effective algorithms and overcoming related difficulties by analyzing and contrasting various algorithms. A quick overview of the state of machine learning algorithms is provided in the review’s first part. It shows a wide context of learning algorithms, such as supervised, unsupervised, semisupervised, and reinforcement. Each algorithm is displayed in accordance with its definition, scalability, performance, applications, advantages, and disadvantages. It is also exhibited in relation to its challenges, which are also mandatory portions that are detailed in a distinct section. Furthermore, the review paper also offers predictions for future perspectives and emerging trends in the machine-learning industry.

articleTitle: Integrating BERT with Recurrent Neural Networks for Predictive Analytics in Product Safety and Reliability Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: In the domain of product safety and reliability engineering, predictive analytics plays a crucial role in identifying potential failures and ensuring high-quality manufacturing standards. This study explores the integration of Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) with Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to enhance predictive capabilities in assessing product reliability. BERT, renowned for its powerful natural language processing (NLP) capabilities, is employed to extract meaningful features from textual data, such as engineering documentation and failure logs. These features are then combined with sequential data processed by RNNs, which excel in capturing temporal dependencies and patterns in time-series data. The combined approach leverages BERT’s contextual understanding to improve feature representation and RNN’s strength in modeling sequences to predict internal failures more accurately. The Bosch Production Line Performance dataset serves as the foundation for this research, providing extensive measurements and test results from various stages of the assembly line. The integration of BERT and RNNs allows for a comprehensive analysis of both textual and numerical data, enabling the prediction of component failures and optimization of manufacturing processes. This hybrid model achieves a predictive accuracy of 98.5% and delivers actionable insights to enhance product safety and reliability.By combining advanced NLP techniques with robust sequence modeling, this study offers a novel approach to tackling complex predictive challenges in product engineering, ultimately contributing to more reliable and cost-effective manufacturing practices.

articleTitle: High-Accuracy Animal Species Classification Using Transfer Learning with ResNet50 on Wildlife Camera Trap Images for Enhanced Conservation Efforts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: Accurately identifying animal species from wildlife camera trap images is essential for conservation and biodiversity monitoring. However, manual processing is severely constrained by the massive volume of data collected by camera traps. Using transfer learning and the ResNet50 model, a high-accura cy animal species classification framework was offered as an approach to this challenge. Utilization of the iWildCam2020_256 dataset—a varied collection of wildlife photos taken in a range of ecosystems optimize ResNet50, a pre-trained neural network to improve its performance on this particular job. With the use of transfer learning approaches, this approach aims to maximize the model's feature extraction capabilities and make it capable of accurately differentiating between a large number of animal species. Compared with traditional techniques, the suggested framework significantly improved classification accuracy when trained and verified on the iWildCam2020_256 dataset. the application of data augmentation techniques and network hyperparameter tuning to reduce overfitting and enhance generalization in various contexts. The outcomes show how well the model can classify species in difficult situations, like changing lighting and partial occlusions. By offering a reliable instrument for automated species identification, our study advances the area of animal conservation by enabling more effective and scalable biodiversity assessments. With a 97% accuracy score, the suggested framework performs remarkably well and shows consistent species recognition across a wide range of animal images. It is essential to include the suggested framework into conservation initiatives, which would help with the precise and timely monitoring of wildlife populations—a crucial component in maintaining biodiversity.

articleTitle: Transformer based Deep Learning Model for Underwater Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: A parallel-guided underwater image improvement technique utilising a Transformer and CNN is suggested to rectify low contrast and colour distortion in underwater images. The approach employs a 3D position embedding model to furnish the Transformer with relative positional data, colour distortion metrics, and global characteristics of the feature map. A CNN encoder extracts local image features, while global features obtained from the Transformer are combined with the CNN-extracted local features via a feature modulation matrix. The CNN decoder enhances the image resolution, and the resulting feature map is input into a feature enhancement network, which produces the final output. The algorithm is trained using the current EUVP paired dataset. To validate the algorithm's superiority, underwater images exhibiting varied levels of colour distortion were chosen for qualitative comparison and quantitative analysis. The findings indicate that the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of the enhanced underwater images surpass those of alternative comparison algorithms, with a notable enhancement in subjective quality, resulting in images characterised by more vibrant colours and greater clarity.

articleTitle: Investigating Boiling Heat Transfer in Extreme Environments from the Deep Sea to Outer Space
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: The Adaptive Thermal Exchange Algorithm (ATEA) is a revolutionary approach to transfer the most heated heat across hard conditions like the deepest ocean or the empty space between the stars. ATEA uses deep-sea adaptation and space resilience optimization to improve performance, durability, and adaptability. ATEA can modify heat flow on the fly, making it useful in many weather situations. For durability, material qualities vary constantly. This ensures spacecraft parts are robust under harsh environments. ATEA alters cooking parameters in real time based on environmental feedback, making it unique. The study compares ATEA to traditional approaches using efficiency, lifespan, and adaptability. The data demonstrate that ATEA works better, changing how individuals handle difficult situations. ATEA might revolutionize space and deep-sea research, as shown by this paper. This study explains how boiling heat flows in tough conditions and provides a meaningful response that other approaches cannot. Environmental science, marine biology, and aviation engineering benefit from the discoveries.

articleTitle: Intelligent Security Scheme for Backdoor Attacks in High Speed Heterogeneous Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: In the realm of cyber security within multi-user intelligent dynamic spectrum access (DSA) environments, Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a potent decision-making tool. Despite its capabilities, the inherent lack of interpretability in DRL's deep neural networks creates vulnerabilities, notably to backdoor attacks. This research delves into DSA in heterogeneous networks and proposes a subtle, yet effective method for executing backdoor attacks. The approach involves an attacker discreetly monitoring channel usage to select unobtrusive backdoor triggers, which are then slyly embedded into the training data of secondary users during the DRL model's training phase. In the model's operational or inference phase, the attacker can then activate these embedded backdoors. This activation manipulates the secondary users' behaviors, compelling them to execute specific actions that hinder their ability to successfully access communication channels. Simulations conducted as part of this research demonstrate the high efficacy of this backdoor attack method, achieving over a 90% success rate in varying DSA scenarios. This method is not only effective but also efficient, reducing the overhead associated with continuous attacks by 20% to 30%. Remarkably, the approach proves versatile, being applicable across three different DRL model types. These findings underscore a crucial aspect of DRL application in cyber-secure environments, especially in the context of dynamic spectrum access, where the balance of advanced functionality and cyber cyber security is essential.

articleTitle: Harnessing the Synergy Between Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain for Enhancing Transparency Security
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: In the recommended technique, AI and blockchain technology improve system stability and projected maintenance. This innovative technique begins with sensor data collection and preprocessing. This covers cleaning, normalizing, and extracting characteristics for AI model training. The model’s projections set alarming limitations. These are securely stored on a blockchain for data transparency. Continuous feedback loops make data processing safer and enhance model prediction. Combining monitor data with model projections to identify problems and provide effective solutions makes the system more trustworthy. Adaptive beamforming improves optical communication by changing beamforming weights and channel responses in real time, enhancing signal integrity and performance. The technique enhances transparency, security, automation efficiency, scalability, portability, data integrity, privacy protection, system speed, resource usage, fault tolerance, cost-effectiveness, and user experience. Simple, safe, and effective system management and predictive maintenance are demonstrated by their consistently higher performance than prior methods. AI and blockchain work together to establish a new standard by eliminating current constraints and changing all elements.

articleTitle: From mmWave to THz Tracing Frequency Adventures in NGMA-Empowered Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: We suggest using DASANTC to improve spectrum allocation and management in the terahertz (THz) frequency range for next-generation wireless communication systems enabled by NGMA. Innovative algorithms let DASANTC dynamically assign THz spectrum resources for efficient, dependable, and flexible communication services. This innovative technique can quickly adapt to changing network circumstances, user needs, and environmental elements, making it ideal for wireless communication. DASANTC algorithms include three essential parts. Algorithm 1 (DSSE) uses spectrum analyzers in NGMA transceivers to identify and estimate the THz spectrum in real time. DSSE analyzes power spectral density (PSD) and interference to find and utilize idle THz frequencies. Second, the adaptive spectrum allocation and channel assignment (ASACA) algorithm dynamically distributes THz spectrum channels and spectrum depending on the DSSE results. ASACA distributes THz channels to user devices using combinatorial optimization to optimize signal quality, interference reduction, and bandwidth distribution. Algorithm 3: Dynamic Spectrum Management and Adaptation (DSMA) completes the process by monitoring network and user needs. It improves network performance by proactively changing spectrum allocation and channel assignments using reinforcement learning. In new communication systems, DASANTC outperforms standard methods. It has the lowest latency and highest spectral efficiency of the techniques tested. It may transmit more data on the same bandwidth. DASANTC's lowest bit error rate (BER) among all examined systems proves its reliability and error-free nature. Many communication contexts might apply this technique due to its high data rate, wide coverage, and low power consumption.

articleTitle: An Optimized Deep Learning Model For Photographic Images And Photorealistic Computer-Generated Graphics Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: The differentiation between computer-generated images and photographs has emerged as a significant study issue in the image forensics field due to the heightened visual realism of artificial images. Existing research on distinguishing these images typically needs a superior quantity of labeled data for training, high computational resources, and also suffers from inaccurate distinction as well as image quality issues. Therefore, an Adaptive Gazelle Optimization Algorithm Enabled Deep convolutional neural network model (AdGO-DCNN) is developed in this research to resolve the existing difficulties. The DCNN classifier distinguishes the images effectively while reducing the risk of overfitting. The Adaptive Gazelle Optimization (AdGO) helps in the model’s performance improvement with minimized computational time. The experimental outcomes of the research show an excellent performance for the proposed model indicating the model’s efficiency in distinguishing computer-generated and photograph images by attaining an accuracy of 96.54%, 0.09 False negative rate (FNR), 0.07 False positive rate (FPR), 97.04% F-score, 95.18% Precision, and 98.98% recall and 0.964 ROC exceeded other existing approaches.

articleTitle: Challenges and Opportunities in Streaming Data for Quantum Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: There are new quantum data streaming security possibilities and problems. Quantum Key Distribution is the best way to keep streaming data safe. This puts to rest worries about quantum security flaws. For safe key sharing, real-time key distribution, and quantum stability, QKD is the way to go. Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), which uses entanglement, superposition, and uncertainty, is what our approach is based on. This makes encryption and key sharing safer. What we use most often for QKD are BB84, E91, and B92. Our way uses the BB84 protocol, which is an early quantum key distribution (QKD) idea that lets you safely share keys using quantum bits. To send keys over long distances, E91 uses entanglement and Bell state measures. Using a limited set of quantum states, the realistic QKD B92 algorithm makes sure that key sharing is safe. Our method is better than standard encryption when it comes to making keys quickly, protecting against quantum attacks, working over longer distances, being easy to apply, distributing keys in real time, and protecting against quantum threats. Now that we live in the age of quantum awareness, these traits are great for protecting data.

articleTitle: Harnessing the Potential of Infobyte Imprints to Shape Future Digital Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: In this age of rapid technological advancement, how humans and computers interact has altered. Interfaces have evolved from modest beginnings to gateways to a world of information and intelligence as the digital world becomes more complex. This innovative tour was inspired by "Infobyte Imprints," which implies digital information presented in fresh, simple ways. This study delves into the new approach of using Infobyte Imprints to influence the design of future digital user interfaces. Our approach incorporates a wide range of AI and ML methods, such as Natural Language Processing (NLP), Computer Vision (CV), and Reinforcement Learning (RL). Infobyte Imprints are digital fingerprints that are deployed in real-time inside digital interfaces after undergoing data preprocessing, model training, and deployment. The research shows that the suggested technique outperforms 10 other baseline methods in terms of user involvement and productivity. The findings are graphically shown using four different diagram forms. The study topic is summed up in ten keywords that are listed in alphabetical order.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Mobile App for Recreational Suitability Analysis of Beach Locations in India
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: This study focuses on the development of a smartphone application that use the INCOIS (Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services) API to provide real-time information associated with the degree of suitability and safety in the beaches. An important objective of this study is to help visiting tourists in India by providing information regarding weather forecasts, water quality, and warnings regarding the hazards at the coastal regions. It offers real-time alerts, support for multiple languages, and access even if the user is not connected to the internet with modern mobile development frameworks like Flutter and React Native in combination with Python and Node.js in the backend. The outcome of the initiative would be that safety to both the tourist and the authorities would be enhanced besides overall improvement in beach experience.

articleTitle: Clustering and Optimization Techniques for Enhanced Segmentation in Retail
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: Customer segmentation is a critical factor of current retail strategies, empowering businesses to recognize various customer behaviors, preferences, and requirements. Traditional segmentation approaches such as demographic, geographic, and behavioral approaches often decrease rapid in seizing the complication of customer communications, specifically in the phase of big data. This research explores the progress of an optimized segmentation technique using K-means clustering for the retail industry. By leveraging machine learning and big data analytics, the training reports key challenges, including the understanding of K-means clustering to original centroids and the impact of outliers on cluster accurateness.The research services a wide-ranging data collection approach that participates multiple data sources, with point-of-sale (POS) systems, customer relationship management (CRM) tools, and operational behavior pursuing. These various datasets provide a comprehensive view of customer communications and are used to create diverse customer segments. The K-means algorithm is then optimized using approaches such as K-means++ loading to improve centroid collection and minimize clustering errors. The Elbow Technique is functional to regulate the optimum number of clusters, certifying the balance between cluster accurateness and computational productivity. The results validate that the optimized segmentation technique provides more correct and criminal understandings compared to traditional methods. Retailers can use these insights to initial marketing campaigns, enhance customer involvements, and improve inventory management. The study concludes that machine learning-driven segmentation models, when properly optimized, meaningfully improve retail operations and customer engagement, concrete the way for more data-driven decision making in the industry. Future research will focus on active additional clustering algorithms and increasing the model to real-time data environments.

articleTitle: Development of Scalable Deep Learning Frameworks Utilizing Advanced Hybrid Models like Transformer-CNN for Distributed Computing Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: Over the past few years especially in the context of communication and information processing the importance of Natural language processing which demands efficient deep learning models has rapidly increased with the complexity of language data and the performance requirements in the distributed computing environment. Popular classical machine learning models fail to capture the contextual relations between words in language data deteriorating their performance in complex tasks. Previous approaches have improved significantly when the use of transformers was adopted in the feature extraction of context but still proposes a problem when it comes to feature extraction at scale in a distributed environment. Therefore, in this research, a new model utilizing both the deep contextual understanding of BERT and the hierarchical feature extraction capabilities of CNN is presented to overcome these difficulties. This combined approach is proposed to improve the model’s efficiency in the classification of text data with focus on scalability when applied in distributed systems. To address the issue, the suggested model was put into practice and examined using Python; the computed outcomes revealed a 99.1% accuracy level. The combination of BERT’s contextual embeddings are fused with CNN’s feature extraction not only increases the efficiency in the predictive accuracy but also the generalization of this model for the various text classification applications. This paper demonstrates the possibility of developing new hybrid models that can help improve the current state of the natural language processing field and suggest areas for future research in the development and utilization of these models in practical applications.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Next-Generation Industry with AI-Blockchain Synergy for Enhanced Security and Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: AI and blockchain are making future enterprises safer, more automated, and more open. This article proposes combining machine learning algorithms with open blockchain networks to improve corporate operations and protect private data. We tried using it for safe industrial processes, smart contract-based banking, and autonomous supply chain management. Technology performance, transaction speed, data loss, and cost were the KPIs. The trial found that blockchain's safety reduced data breaches by 41%, automation improved by 38%, and smart contracts ran 23% quicker. Technology reduced operational expenses by 27% compared to conventional methods. A detailed scalability analysis demonstrated that the proposed system could handle 1.5 million events per second and make 99.9% accurate automated judgments. Data shows that merging AI with blockchain makes things safer, more automated, and cheaper, making it a smart choice for digital-first companies.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Centralized System for Street Light Automation Light and Fault Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: Electricity is a very high-scale need for the modern world and effective public lighting infrastructure ensures safety and security in urban regions. Traditional methods of street light maintenance appear to be inefficient and cumbersome in Indian cities. The proposed system provides an "IoT-Based Centralized System for Street Light Fault Detection and Street Light Automation" to enhance the maintenance capabilities of the public lighting infrastructure. The system utilizes the advanced IoT technology understanding superior fault detection algorithms such as threshold-based activation and faults using light sensors and LED status monitoring. Such techniques enable real-time monitoring and automatic street light faults. It will help in providing data-driven insights that allow for efficient maintenance operations, prevent downtime, and control costs related to operations. This will be helpful for the line men to track down the street lights and correct them easily. Most important, it saves energy, thereby making it sustainable in the use of energy. Overall, the proposed system is a significant step ahead in the management of urban lighting with scalable solutions to enhance operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for Real-Time Object Detection and Classification in IoT-Enabled Smart Bins for Efficient E-Waste Collection and Sorting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: The rapid growth of electronic waste (e-waste) poses significant environmental and logistical challenges, as discarded electronics contain valuable resources and hazardous materials. Effective management and recycling of e-waste are essential to mitigate environmental impact and recover valuable materials. This is a very important factor in the light of the fact that the generation of e-waste is currently on the rise. To the best of our knowledge, this paper puts forward a new technique for efficient Real-time Object Detection and Classification in Smart IoT bins using CNNs which is implemented using python and accuracy is 98%. The proposed system incorporates the most recent CNN algorithms in order to tag and sort e-waste items as they are placed in the smart bins. The building enable the use of modern CNN models like Faster R-CNN, YOLO and SSD for real-time image analysis on the bin’s camera system. These models are subsequently refined using a large dataset of e-waste images to increase the models’ capabilities of identifying different electronic parts and gadgets. It also comprising a light-weight edge compute architecture so that the object detection, as well as its classification, can happen at a very fast speed thereby eliminating the delays inherent in feedback. Using IoT technology in the smart bins allows the bins to connect to the waste management system to relay details of the type and amount of e-waste being dumped. It helps in decisions to be made as to which direction to take the collection trucks, as well as sorting procedures to be followed at recycling facilities.

articleTitle: Empirical Studies on Wearable WSNs in Human Activity Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: Our research study, "Wearable WSNs in Human Activity Recognition," describes a complete method for detecting human activity using wireless sensor networks and wearable devices. Gathering and processing data, extracting characteristics, and applying them are three techniques to identify movement. We test with several WSN-equipped persons. Our portable WSNs include accelerometers, gyroscopes, and heart rate monitors to collect and analyze data. Continuously filtering and altering raw sensor data prepares it for usage. Feature extraction is essential to interpret mixed sensor data. No more MAD or Fast Fourier Transform. We identify human behavior using Random Forest, K-NN, and LSTM Network techniques. Our WSNHAR approach outperforms others in "Comparison of Recognition Metrics" and "Computational Efficiency and Energy Consumption" charts. Memory, F1-score, precision, accuracy, and processing time indicate system speed. The recommended approach computes swiftly and uses little power, making it suitable for energy-efficient programs.
